issues.description: The template Farm.java defines the helper method singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), while the problem statement UML and the reference solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This mismatch is structural: students following the specification will implement and call singFarmSongVerse with an Animal, but the template's signature prevents that and may confuse or block their implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the Animal parameter in the template method signature to match the specification and solution: change singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and update its implementation to use the passed-in animal (e.g. animal.getClass().getSimpleName() and animal.messageOnFeed()). This preserves the intended design and prevents student confusion.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal):boolean (indicating a boolean return), but the reference solution implements addAnimal(Animal) as void. The template Farm.java also does not provide an addAnimal implementation. This mismatch between the problem UML and the actual implementation/signature in the solution can confuse students who expect addAnimal to return a boolean based on the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make signatures consistent. Either change the problem UML to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal):void (so it matches the solution), or modify the solution (and template) so addAnimal returns boolean as specified in the UML (and document the meaning of the returned boolean).
